pilot.arithmetic: compiled __int128 modular multiplication with plain remainder
pilot.timing_statistic: median aggregate wall ns per work-prime update
pilot.parallel_workers: all workers visible to the allocated pilot node

incremental_accounting.definition: For each source family, modulus, weight profile, and prime, initialize p(k)=1 once; visit dimensions in order; update every p(k) once; emit the current prefix residue; never restart a prefix from dimension one.
incremental_accounting.count_includes: all work-prime incremental product updates for both fidelity families plus nonduplicated usability profiles
count_excludes: two universal overflow-check primes per run

correctness_required: all selected prefix residues match the Python modular oracle
all two overflow primes are evaluated for every emitted prefix
production_decision.authorize_full_exact_fidelity_grid_iff: correctness passes AND projected_node_days<=7 AND replay_overhead_fraction<=0.15

no_go_fallback.tier_boundary_rule: After measurement, choose the largest global d_cut in [16,3600] for which the same measured median ns/update projects the complete two-family fidelity workload through d_cut, plus the frozen usability workload, to at most 7 node-days. The rule is applied mechanically before any production merit is inspected.
no_go_fallback.dimensions_at_or_below_cut: exact rational or sufficient CRT residues
no_go_fallback.arb_precision_escalation: double precision until the radius predicate passes

replay_failure_disposition.action: do not authorize exact or two-tier production; redesign streaming/checkpoint implementation and rerun under a new preregistration

artifact_geometry.consumer_download_expectation: approximately 2-3 GB before compression and manifest metadata; chunk-selective verification is supported

paper_perimeter_sentence: Across the frozen distribution sites and the named, hash-frozen six-paper primary-literature perimeter, we found no numerical merit attached to the frozen vectors; this is not a universal claim about the QMC literature.
